# Transactions and sessions

## Managed and unmanaged

```ts
await sequelize.transaction(async (transaction) => {
  await Account.decrement('balance', { by: 30, where: { owner: 'ann' }, transaction });
  await Account.increment('balance', { by: 30, where: { owner: 'bob' }, transaction });
});

const failed = await sequelize
  .transaction(async (transaction) => {
    await Account.update({ balance: 0 }, { where: {}, transaction });
    throw new Error('abort');
  })
  .catch((error: Error) => error.message);
// failed === 'abort'; the update was rolled back
```

```ts
const transaction = await sequelize.transaction({
  isolationLevel: Transaction.ISOLATION_LEVELS.REPEATABLE_READ,
});
const committed: string[] = [];
transaction.afterCommit(() => {
  committed.push(transaction.id);
});
try {
  await Account.create({ owner: 'cid', balance: 5 }, { transaction });
  await transaction.commit();
} catch (error) {
  await transaction.rollback();
  throw error;
}
```

## Savepoints

```ts
await sequelize.transaction(async (outer) => {
  await Account.create({ owner: 'dan', balance: 1 }, { transaction: outer });
  await sequelize
    .transaction({ transaction: outer }, async (inner) => {
      await Account.create({ owner: 'eve', balance: 1 }, { transaction: inner });
      throw new Error('rolls back to the savepoint only');
    })
    .catch(() => undefined);
});
// dan is saved, eve is not
```

## Row locks

```ts
const holder = await sequelize.transaction();
await Account.findAll({ where: { owner: 'ann' }, lock: true, transaction: holder });

const free = await sequelize.transaction((worker) =>
  Account.findAll({ lock: Transaction.LOCK.UPDATE, skipLocked: true, transaction: worker }),
);
const noWait = await sequelize
  .transaction((worker) =>
    Account.findAll({ where: { owner: 'ann' }, lock: true, noWait: true, transaction: worker }),
  )
  .catch((error: unknown) => error);
await holder.rollback();
// free: every row except ann's; noWait: DatabaseError (could not obtain lock)
```

Lock only named tables (needed with an optional `include`):

```ts
const Entry = sequelize.define('Entry', { memo: DataTypes.TEXT }, { timestamps: false });
Account.hasMany(Entry, { as: 'entries', foreignKey: 'accountId' });
await Entry.sync();

const locked = await sequelize.transaction(async (tx) => {
  // FOR NO KEY UPDATE OF "Account": the outer-joined entries stay unlocked.
  const accounts = await Account.findAll({
    include: [{ model: Entry, as: 'entries' }],
    lock: { level: Transaction.LOCK.NO_KEY_UPDATE, of: 'Account' },
    skipLocked: true,
    transaction: tx,
  });
  return accounts.length;
});
```

## CLS

```ts
Sequelize.useCLS(); // global switch: managed transactions now apply to queries inside the callback
await sequelize.transaction(async () => {
  await User.update({ active: true }, { where: {} }); // runs in the transaction, no option needed
});
```

## Settings, LISTEN/NOTIFY, advisory locks

```ts
const user = await sequelize.transaction(
  { settings: { 'app.user_id': 42, statement_timeout: '5s' } },
  (transaction) =>
    sequelize.query("SELECT current_setting('app.user_id') AS id", {
      type: QueryTypes.SELECT,
      plain: true,
      transaction,
    }),
);
// user: { id: '42' }; the settings end with the transaction (SET LOCAL semantics)
```

```ts
const received: string[] = [];
const unlisten = await sequelize.listen('jobs', (payload, channel) => {
  received.push(`${channel}: ${payload ?? ''}`);
});

await sequelize.notify('jobs', { id: 1 });
await sequelize.transaction(async (transaction) => {
  await Job.create({ name: 'export', state: 'queued' }, { transaction });
  await sequelize.notify('jobs', 'export queued', { transaction }); // delivered on commit
});
await pause(200);
await unlisten();
// received: ['jobs: {"id":1}', 'jobs: export queued']
```

```ts
const holder = await sequelize.transaction();
await holder.advisoryLock('jobs:42');

const other = await sequelize.transaction();
const busy = await other.tryAdvisoryLock('jobs:42'); // false: held by `holder`
const free = await other.tryAdvisoryLock(7); // true: integer keys work too
await holder.commit(); // transaction-level locks are released on commit / rollback
await other.rollback();
```

```ts
const paired = await sequelize.transaction(async (transaction) => {
  await transaction.advisoryLock(7, 42); // pg_advisory_xact_lock(7, 42)
  const shared = await transaction.tryAdvisoryLock(7, 43, { shared: true });

  await transaction.advisoryLock(7, 44, { session: true });
  const released = await transaction.advisoryUnlock(7, 44);
  return shared && released;
});
```

Routing connections (v6 `sequelize.connectionManager`): every query, transaction, COPY and `sync` takes its connection from `connectionManager.getConnection(options?)` and returns it through `connectionManager.releaseConnection(connection)`, looked up at call time, so both can be reassigned on the instance (for example to pick a database per request from an `AsyncLocalStorage`):

```ts
const shardOfRequest = new AsyncLocalStorage<string>();
const shards: Record<string, Sequelize> = { b: shard };
const manager = sequelize.connectionManager;
const defaultGet = manager.getConnection.bind(manager);
const defaultRelease = manager.releaseConnection.bind(manager);
const owners = new WeakMap<object, Sequelize>();

manager.getConnection = async (options) => {
  const target = shards[shardOfRequest.getStore() ?? ''];
  if (target === undefined) {
    return defaultGet(options);
  }
  const connection = await target.connectionManager.getConnection(options);
  owners.set(connection, target); // remember which pool the connection must go back to
  return connection;
};
manager.releaseConnection = (connection) => {
  const owner = owners.get(connection);
  return owner === undefined
    ? defaultRelease(connection)
    : owner.connectionManager.releaseConnection(connection);
};

const applicationName = async (): Promise<string> => {
  const rows = (await sequelize.query('SHOW application_name', {
    type: QueryTypes.SELECT,
  })) as { application_name: string }[];
  return rows[0]?.application_name ?? '';
};
routed = [
  await applicationName(), // no routing value: the instance's own pool
  await shardOfRequest.run('b', applicationName), // routed to the other instance's pool
  await shardOfRequest.run('b', () => sequelize.transaction(() => applicationName())),
];
// routed: ['', 'shard-b', 'shard-b']
```

Keep acquire/release paired and release a connection to the pool that owns it (it may come from another `Sequelize` instance's manager). `listen` uses its own dedicated connection and is not routed.

Raw connections and pool gauges: `getConnection({ type: 'read' })` returns a replica connection (writer without `replication` or with `useMaster`), `releaseConnection(c)` returns it to its own pool, `destroyConnection(c)` drops a broken one (the pool opens a replacement on demand), and `connectionManager.pool` gives live `size`, `available`, `using`, `waiting`, `maxSize` (with `replication`: totals plus `pool.read` / `pool.write`):

```ts
const manager = replicated.connectionManager;
const { pool } = manager; // live counters: size, available, using, waiting, maxSize

// A raw connection held outside any query; `type: 'read'` takes a replica.
const reader = await manager.getConnection({ type: 'read' });
const readerUsing = pool.read?.using; // 1: the replicas' pools, `pool.write?.using` is 0
try {
  await reader.query('SELECT 1');
  await manager.releaseConnection(reader); // back to the replica pool it came from
} catch (error) {
  await manager.destroyConnection(reader); // a broken connection: closed, never reused
  throw error;
}
// pool: { size: 1, available: 1, using: 0, waiting: 0 }
```

Retry (v6 `retry`): `new Sequelize({ retry: { max: 5, match: [/SequelizeConnectionRefusedError/], backoffBase: 100 } })` or per query `{ retry: {...} }` (merged over the instance option) repeats a failed query, and the connection acquisition plus `BEGIN` of a transaction. Nothing is retried without `max`; an empty `match` retries every error; a statement inside an open transaction, `COMMIT`, COPY and `listen` are never retried.

```ts
const retry = {
  max: 5, // attempts, the first one included
  match: [/SequelizeConnectionRefusedError/, 'ECONNRESET'], // retry only these errors
  backoffBase: 10, // ms before the first retry; grows by backoffExponent (default 1.1)
};
const refusing = new Sequelize({
  database,
  username,
  password,
  host,
  port,
  logging: false,
  dialectOptions: sequelize.options.dialectOptions,
  retry, // every query and transaction start of this instance
});

// Simulate a database that refuses the first two connections.
const manager = refusing.connectionManager;
const getConnection = manager.getConnection.bind(manager);
manager.getConnection = async (options) => {
  attempts += 1;
  if (attempts <= 2) {
    throw new ConnectionRefusedError(new Error('connect ECONNREFUSED'));
  }
  return getConnection(options);
};

retried = await refusing.query('SELECT 1 AS one', { type: QueryTypes.SELECT, plain: true });
// retried: { one: 1 }, attempts: 3

// A query can override the instance setting; a statement inside a transaction is never retried.
await refusing.query('SELECT 1', { retry: { max: 2 } });
await refusing.close();
```

Read replicas: `new Sequelize({ replication: { read: [...], write } })` routes reads to replicas; see <https://tormozz48.github.io/postgrelize/guide/sessions>.
